text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices spiked sharply on escalating geopolitical tension. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint through which roughly a third of the world's seaborne oil passes, pushing crude prices higher and boosting the outlook for an oil producer's earnings and cash flow.

The two-week rally of 15.6% reflects a broader shift in the oil market: physical crude has become much more expensive to move due to surging tanker rates (adding roughly $38 a barrel to delivery costs), and geopolitical risk in the Middle East is keeping prices elevated. Brent crude, the global benchmark, sits at $126.55 per barrel while U.S. crude is at $101.91—a gap that widens when supply risks flare up, as they have this week.
